leverage.exposure: No leverage is open. The balance is positive, the squad is at the minimum rather than above it, and no offer is outstanding, so there is nothing that has to be unwound before the lock. The risk this run is entirely about the keeper slot scoring zero, not about the balance.

binding_gap: The binding gap is the goalkeeper, and it is unfixable this matchday. It is not a cash problem in the ordinary sense — spending power is ample on paper — but an unwind problem: the only upgrade cannot be paid for and unwound back to a non-negative balance with eleven players before the lock. After the keeper, the second gap is the cheap Mainz defender, who is a fielded body with a near-worthless scoring average; both gaps are next-matchday work, funded by the tick trade that reopens tonight.

verdict.headline: No action.
verdict.detail: No action. The squad is at exactly eleven, all placed, balance positive, and the only legal formation is already set — so there is nothing to sell without taking the under-eleven penalty and nothing on the board that can be bought and unwound before the lock. This is the fifth consecutive quiet run and the position has not moved. The one thing that changed is informational: Kompany's pre-Leipzig press conference is this morning, well before the lock, which corrects the standing ledger claim that Georg would have to set this matchday blind on the keeper. Even so, the presser cannot change what he does — every goalkeeper alternative is either a confirmed non-starter or leaves a negative balance at lock, which would zero the entire matchday.

sell.reason: No sale is possible or advisable. At exactly eleven players, any sale drops the fielded side below the minimum and takes the flat penalty, which outweighs every value argument on the board. The standing instruction not to sell the keeper also holds: the slot is uninsurable, and the alternatives all score the same as an injured keeper while costing a roster slot.

buy.reason: No buy is possible for this matchday. Only four board listings expire before the lock, and only one of them — the Hoffenheim keeper — is a genuine starter and a genuine upgrade. He is still short by a little over two million after selling the current keeper back at market value, which would leave a negative balance at the lock and score zero for the whole matchday. Adding a second sale closes less than half the gap and drops the squad to ten. Every manager ask on the board is priced above market value, which this ledger has never treated as a buy. The remaining pre-lock listings are a never-played Mainz backup keeper, a Schalke forward and a cheap Dortmund defender, none of whom improves a fielded slot. Everything else on the board, including the Bayern defender listed overnight and the Freiburg defender whose block conditions are partly met, expires after the lock and is a next-matchday question, not this one.

movers.reason: No flip is possible, and the reason is mechanical rather than a pricing judgement. The next market-value tick lands after the lock, so no listing bought now can capture a tick before this matchday scores, while the cash it absorbs would leave a negative balance at the lock. The edge itself is intact and has not decayed: rising-flag players still rose at the next tick in roughly nine cases out of ten, on a sample that has kept growing, and falling-flag players still fell. Rivals continue to harvest it at scale — one manager churned four sales and a buy inside seven minutes overnight, and that buy cleared in the low single digits over market value, consistent with the low cluster. The flip window reopens after tonight's tick, for the next matchday. Two questions remain open and unresolved: whether Kickbase caps squad size, which would cap how many flips can run at once, and the fact that this edge is measured in one league over one period and will decay if enough rivals crowd into it.

fitness.sweep: The keeper is the only squad player flagged, and the news got firmer rather than better: a dated probable eleven published yesterday names the backup in goal and calls him only doubtful. That is the first source that actively replaces him rather than merely doubting him. The decisive moment is this morning's press conference, which lands hours before the lock — the next run is too early to read it, the one after is the first that can. The other ten are clean: none appears on the league-wide injured-and-suspended table, and nine of them are named in their club's probable eleven. The exception is the cheap Mainz defender, who is absent from his club's probable eleven — a selection problem, not a fitness one, and one that has been true all season.
